title: [Kernel] Consolidate Marlin thread-tile padding across all dense Marlin paths
body:
## Purpose

Marlin GEMM/repack require the rank-local (N, K) to match a thread-tile family: (n%64, k%128) or (n%128, k%64). TP sharding can produce shapes satisfying neither — FP4/FP8 paths crash at repack (e.g. `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-NVFP4` at TP4) and GPTQ/AWQ/WNA16 reject Marlin and fall back to slower kernels.

Fix: zero-pad weights/scales to the nearest valid tile with one shared mechanism (`marlin_padded_nk` + pad helpers in `marlin_utils.py`), used by all Marlin surfaces — FP4/MXFP4, FP8/MXFP8, GPTQ/AWQ/WNA16 (`MarlinLinearKernel`), and NVFP4 MoE. Apply-time code recovers the padded extents from the packed weight shape, so nothing is threaded through new kwargs or layer attributes. Aligned shapes take the same code path as before; act-order and groups straddling TP ranks keep the strict checks.

## Motivation

The `ConsistentHashRing::get_owners` method is called frequently during rate-limit checks. The previous implementation allocated a new `HashSet` and cloned multiple `String`s for every lookup. In Qwen3.5 GDN layers the input projection is issued as two separate GEMMs, `in_proj_qkvz` and

DeepSeek-V4.1 uses a hierarchical sparse indexer in its decoder:

- Layer 20 performs a full-context index scan and publishes up to 16,384 candidate positions.
